$comment: Conformance entries this grammar cannot decide, with the reason for each.
All five are negative syntax tests, and four of them have a better answer
than a parse error: `variablesInDataBlocks(state)` hands a linter the span
of the offending variable, so `DATA { :s :p ?o }` can underline `?o` and
say why instead of marking the whole block red.
The list is asserted exactly: an entry that starts passing must be removed
here, and an entry that stops passing is a failing build.

srl-syntax.test_113: An undeclared prefix. Whether `:s` resolves is a question about the prologue, not about the shape of the document.
srl-syntax.test_122: A variable as the object of a ground DATA triple. Expressing this needs a third parallel triples hierarchy for one rule; `variablesInDataBlocks()` reports it with the variable's own span instead.
srl-syntax.test_123: A variable as the predicate of a ground DATA triple, as above.
srl-syntax.test_124: A variable as the subject of a ground DATA triple, as above.
srl-syntax.test_126: A variable reifier in a ground DATA triple, as above.
